newsitem.title: UK: LIFFE cocoa ends soft despite strong U.S. grinds.
newsitem.headline: LIFFE cocoa ends soft despite strong U.S. grinds.

text.p: LIFFE cocoa futures ended lower despite stronger-than-expected U.S. grinds.

May closed down four stg at 1,019 stg per tonne and July slipped seven to 1,032. But activity was thin with total volume notching only 2,041 contracts. July was most active with 841 contracts changing hands, followed by December with 353.
First-quarter U.S. grinds jumped 20.74 percent from a year ago, sharply higher than forecasts for flat to up five percent.
CSCE cocoa initially opened stronger on the figures and briefly pulled London up into positive ground, but commission house sales in the afternoon in London pressured prices again, traders said.
But traders said losses were limited by trade buying and the absence of origin selling because of a holiday in the Ivory Coast.
Despite Friday's losses, most traders were still optimistic on cocoa and expected the market to try testing the upside again.

If July hits its April 2 peak of 1,065, traders said fund interest could emerge to give cocoa a further lift. So far, traders noted very little fund rotation into commodities despite recent jitters in financial markets.
But some technical analysts said cocoa was losing upward momentum, and if it did not break higher soon, it would start to drift down again.
July also closed below intial support at 1,020 stg and had an inside trading day, which could point to another dip on Monday.

Further July support sits at 1,000. More crucial support rests between 987 and the April 9 low of 980. Some said a break of 987 would be enough to turn the market lower, while a break of 980 could lure funds into setting new short positions.
The Ivory Coast minister of commodities' preliminary forecast for the country's mid-crop to be near 100,000 tonnes had little impact on prices. Government forecasts are traditionally conservative.
Market forecasts have ranged from 100,000 to 160,000, still below last year's bumper 200,000-tonne crop.
Switches tightened slightly, with May/July closing near 13 after trading between 15 and 16 earlier this week.
In options, 10 July 1,100 stg calls traded in the afternoon.
